name: Verity Long
life: Verity became a school secretary because records showed her exactly which families needed another reminder before a deadline. In her own divorce she has been much worse at asking people for time. On Tuesday, near the window at Night Shift Donuts, Verity knows when the going-home crowd and the coming-to-work crowd will both be there.
voice: I can afford the house only with a lodger. The owner asked if that meant strangers all the time. I told him a stranger is how my children got the aunt who raised them.
appearance: Verity is easy to recognize by a dark undercut with a longer wave on top and fine brows over wide-set eyes. Usually dressed in a sand-colored linen shirt with a thin silver ring worn on a cord, Verity gathers both sleeves neatly before settling in when listening.
personality: Verity has an appetite for a good argument about little things and works hard to keep a serious disagreement from being turned into entertainment.
agenda: To make a fair room offer to a prospective lodger.
family: Ruth Farah is Verity’s cousin raised in the same household. Verity makes room at the table. Ruth brings whatever was actually growing or affordable that week. The meal sometimes produces a solution. Even when it does not, everyone goes away knowing what the other household is up against. Asked about *Laundry for a stranger*, Ruth says, “I built her an iron rest from a broken tile.”
connections: Ruth Eade. The prospective buyer and agent must decide what a lodger means for the old owner's conditions.

reactions.situation: A buyer offers extra for the porch lamp
reactions.response: Verity asks the owner whether the lamp is even part of the sale before discussing the offer.
